install.detail: From the Stripe App Marketplace, or a direct install link provided by XBorderCo.

Stripe shows an OAuth consent screen. XBorderCo requests read access to customer and subscription data, the ability to create and modify invoices and add invoice line items, and access to webhook events.

Review the configuration changes for your integration type, agree terms, provide business details and tax settings. XBorderCo's webhook goes live at the end of onboarding — the merchant wires up nothing.
Sandbox testing is available on the dev and demo environments.

what_the_merchant_never_does.registrations: The merchant does not register in the countries they sell into. XBorderCo holds the registrations, files and remits.
what_the_merchant_never_does.liability: On sales where XBorderCo acts as the deemed supplier, XBorderCo is the party liable for the tax. The merchant remains the supplier of their own product to their own customer, keeps their Stripe account, their customers and their payouts.
what_the_merchant_never_does.webhooks: The merchant subscribes to nothing. XBorderCo's webhook is activated at the end of onboarding.
what_the_merchant_never_does.integration_work: The merchant's developers do no integration work. XBorderCo applies the configuration for the merchant's integration pattern during onboarding. The merchant tests transactions.
what_the_merchant_never_does.renewals: Existing subscription renewals require no changes — they create draft invoices that XBorderCo amends automatically.

configuration_patterns.pattern: Stripe Checkout, mode: subscription (including Payment Links)
configuration_patterns.first_cycle: Stripe creates and pays the first invoice atomically, and it cannot be amended afterwards. XBorderCo leaves it alone and points the customer at XBorderCo's own tax invoice through the invoice footer, set on the customer record before the first invoice exists. On a frictionless wallet (Apple Pay, Amazon Pay) the sequence can complete before the per-customer footer is in place, in which case the first invoice carries the account-level default footer instead.
configuration_patterns.supersedes: §7.4 tells merchants to add subscription_data.billing_cycle_anchor and proration_behavior to delay the first invoice. 21-subscriptions.md (June 2026) records that approach as not how this works; do not quote the §7.4 version for Checkout or Payment Links.

configuration_patterns.do_not: Do NOT enable invoice_creation.enabled — Stripe finalises the invoice before XBorderCo can amend it.
configuration_patterns.first_cycle: XBorderCo creates the invoice after checkout completes.
The draft is held for XBorderCo to amend, then finalised so payment collects as normal.
configuration_patterns.risk: Omitting auto_advance: false lets the invoice finalise before XBorderCo can process it.

add: billing_cycle_anchor set to a future timestamp
configuration_patterns.first_cycle: The delay lets Stripe create the first invoice as a draft, which XBorderCo then amends.
UNDOCUMENTED — xbc-docs does not give Elements its own configuration guidance. Confirm with XBorderCo rather than assuming it matches Hosted Checkout.

engine_flow: XBorderCo listens for invoice.created. Checkout-originated invoices are handled inline by the checkout path; API and renewal invoices are paused as drafts. Before it acts on any invoice it runs a set of gates: whether the invoice was already processed, whether the merchant and the customer's country are eligible and whether liability sits with XBorderCo, whether every product on the invoice classifies to a supported tax code, and whether a customer tax ID is awaiting verification (in which case the invoice is held rather than processed). Jurisdiction is decided from an evidence hierarchy rather than a single address lookup — the billing address, the payment-instrument country, Stripe's own location signals, and any customer tax ID, with a validated VAT number driving reverse-charge treatment. It then calculates and applies the tax, writes its own sequential tax invoice, and finalises so payment collects as normal. Anything out of scope is restored untouched.
not_supported: PaymentIntents used directly — no invoice is created, so XBorderCo never sees the transaction.
The legacy Charges API — same reason.
Stripe Checkout in mode: payment with invoice_creation.enabled — Stripe finalises the invoice before XBorderCo can amend it.

stripe_tax_comparison.note: Factual, and answerable entirely from Stripe's own documentation. Render it as-is; do not add a recommendation.
stripe_tax_does: Calculates the tax due at checkout.
Monitors your revenue against registration thresholds and tells you where you have crossed one.
stripe_tax_does_not: File returns or remit the money.
Take on the liability — you remain the party liable for the tax, and you appear on the invoice as that party.
xbc_does: Registers, files and remits in the jurisdictions it covers.
Is named as the party liable for the tax on sales where it is the deemed supplier.
